Federal Energy Regulatory Commission

Washington, D.C. 20426

RE:    Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC
       Docket No. ER27-____-000
       Power Purchase Agreement with North Carolina Electric Membership Corporation,
       Rate Schedule No. 773

Dear Secretary Reese:

         Pursuant to Section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”)1 and Part 35 of the Federal
Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“FERC” or “Commission”) regulations,2 Duke Energy
Carolinas, LLC (“DEC”) hereby submits for filing a new power purchase agreement
(“Agreement”) between DEC and North Carolina Electric Membership Corporation (“NCEMC”).
DEC respectfully requests that the Commission accept the Agreement effective as of January 1,
2027, as agreed upon by the Parties,3 without condition or modification. NCEMC’s support for
this filing and the requested effective date is evidenced by NCEMC’s execution of the Agreement.

I.     BACKGROUND

       A.      Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC

         DEC is a wholly owned subsidiary of Duke Energy Corporation and a vertically integrated
electric utility that generates, transmits, distributes, and sells electricity to approximately 2.9
million customers within its 24,000-square-mile franchised service territory in central and western
North Carolina and western South Carolina. DEC currently meets energy demand primarily from
its fleet of electric generation assets amounting to approximately 20,000 megawatts (“MW”) by
purchases of electricity from the open market, and through purchased power contracts with third
parties. Retail service provided by DEC is subject to the regulatory jurisdiction of the North
Carolina Utilities Commission and the Public Service Commission of South Carolina. DEC’s

sales of wholesale energy and capacity and its provision of open-access transmission service are
subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission.

       B.      North Carolina Electric Membership Corporation

        NCEMC is a generation and transmission electric cooperative responsible for the full or
partial power supply requirements of its 25 rural distribution cooperative member-owners that
serve approximately 2.8 million residential, commercial, and industrial consumers throughout the
State of North Carolina. NCEMC distribution cooperative member-owner loads currently are
located within both DEC’s and Duke Energy Progress, LLC’s (“DEP”) balancing areas.4 DEC
and DEP have both provided long-term wholesale power service to NCEMC through various
power purchase agreements on file with FERC, including the Power Supply and Coordination
Agreement between NCEMC and DEP.5

       C.      South River Electric Membership Corporation Load

         As part of its responsibilities as an electric cooperative, NCEMC is required to supply
electric capacity and energy to its member South River Electric Membership Corporation
(“SREMC”), a load serving entity that has committed to providing retail electric service to Vulcan
Elements (“Vulcan”) for Vulcan’s operation of a new rare earth minerals magnet manufacturing
facility being developed in Benson, North Carolina (the “Vulcan Facility”). 6 The Vulcan Facility
is not projected to become fully operational until September 2028 but Vulcan will be ready to
receive retail electric service under the Agreement on January 1, 2027 to support construction
operations. The Agreement will facilitate NCEMC’s commitment to supply wholesale power to
SREMC to serve the Vulcan Facility.




4
       On January 30, 2026, the Commission issued an order authorizing an internal corporate reorganization under
       which DEP will merge with and into DEC, with DEC being the surviving entity (“Internal Reorganization”).
       See Duke Energy Corp., 194 FERC ¶ 61,084 (2026). The anticipated closing date for the Internal
       Reorganization is January 1, 2027. Accordingly, beginning January 1, 2027, it is expected that DEP, and
       DEP’s balancing area, will no longer exist and NCEMC distribution cooperative member-owner loads will
       all be located within DEC’s balancing area.
5
       On July 21, 2026, in Docket No. ER26-3232-000, DEC submitted to the Commission a Ninth Amended and
       Restated Power Supply and Coordination Agreement that, among other things, replaces DEP with DEC as a
       party to agreement in response to the upcoming Internal Reorganization. That submission remains pending
       before the Commission as of the date of this filing.
6
       The Vulcan Facility has secured substantial public and private backing, including securing $1.4 billion in
       financing from the U.S. government and industry sources. See “Vulcan Elements Forges $1.4 Billion
       Partnership with the United States Government and ReElement Technologies to Expand 100% Vertically
       Integrated, Domestic Magnet Supply Chain,” https://vulcanelements.com/company/updates/vulcan-
       elements-forges-1-4-billion (last visited Oct. 25, 2026).
 Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary
October 28, 2026
Page 3



II.    DESCRIPTION OF THE AGREEMENT

        As noted above, DEP and DEC already provide wholesale power supply service to
NCEMC under various power purchase agreements on file with FERC. The Agreement submitted
herein reflects the Parties’ intent and desire to address the power needs of the Vulcan Facility via
a separate and newly negotiated agreement rather than pursuant to an existing power supply
agreement. The Agreement, therefore, contemplates a discrete power-supply arrangement
designed specifically to permit NCEMC to supply SREMC with the power required to serve the
new Vulcan Facility. The Agreement does not modify or otherwise govern the Parties’ existing
power-supply arrangements or other NCEMC or SREMC load. A summary of the key Agreement
provisions is included below.

       A.      Term

       As noted above, the Vulcan Facility is currently expected to be fully commercially
operational by September 2028, but Vulcan seeks to receive retail electric service under the
Agreement on January 1, 2027 to support construction activities. The Agreement will continue
through September 30, 2046, and will automatically renew and extend for additional term(s) of
five years unless three years’ prior written notice of non-renewal is given by either Party before
any such automatic renewal or the Agreement is otherwise terminated pursuant to Section 2.3 of
the Agreement.

       B.      Sales of Capacity and Energy

       Section 4.1 of the Agreement requires DEC to sell and deliver to NCEMC all of the electric
capacity and energy as the Vulcan Facility requires for its operations. The Agreement stipulates
that NCEMC may not use any other electrical capacity and energy resources of any kind, except
for Emergency Generating Resources only during an Emergency Condition, to serve the NCEMC
Large Load 1 Load. DEC is required to supply and deliver energy and capacity to NCEMC in a
manner that is as firm as, or otherwise comparable with the manner in which DEC serves its own
Native Load.

         The rates under the Agreement are single-system, formulaic cost-based rates based on
DEC’s cost of service as the surviving entity following consummation of the Internal
Reorganization as reflected in DEC’s FERC Form 1 data. NCEMC will pay DEC: (i) a Monthly
Demand Charge set forth in Section 6.3 of the Agreement; (ii) a Monthly Energy Charge set forth
in Section 6.4 of the Agreement, and (iii) a Monthly Charge for NCEMC’s coal combustion
residual (“CCR”) costs set forth in Section 6.5 of the Agreement, while DEC will credit to NCEMC
(iv) the Monthly Credit for its Inflation Reduction Act (“IRA”) production tax credit (“PTC”)
benefit set forth in Section 6.7 (discussed below), as trued up pursuant to Section 6.9. The Monthly
Demand Charge will equal the product of (i) the Monthly Billing Demand for the Month (kW) and
(ii) the Monthly Demand Rate ($/kW-Month), minus (iii) the Ancillary Services Credit as set forth
in Sections 6.3 and 6.4.
 Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary
October 28, 2026
Page 4



        For any month in which NCEMC fails to accept delivery of, or to receive the NCEMC
Large Load 1 Load for one or more hours, NCEMC will remain obligated to pay DEC the Monthly
Demand Charge for such month calculated in accordance with Section 6.3 of the Agreement. The
Agreement provides for certain exceptions to this requirement, namely should Vulcan become a
debtor in a bankruptcy proceeding, or following a Force Majeure Event. Moreover, Section 4.7.1
specifies how DEC must reduce NCEMC’s bill for any hour in which DEC fails to satisfy its
delivery obligations, where such failure is not excused under the terms of the Agreement

       C.      Refund Mechanism for IRA Tax Credits

        The Agreement includes a formal mechanism through which DEC will share with NCEMC
the benefits associated with certain investment tax credits (“ITCs”) and PTCs earned and
monetized under the IRA. Duke will use commercially reasonable efforts to first apply such credits
against applicable tax liabilities and, to the extent credits remain, monetize them through sales or
transfers to third parties.

       NCEMC’s ITC benefits will be amortized and reflected through new tax inputs in the
demand rate formula template, consistent with Commission precedent concerning the
normalization of ITC benefits.7 Section 6.9 and Exhibit IV of the Agreement provide that
NCEMC’s PTC benefit will be returned separately through a monthly invoice credit, net of
reasonable transaction and compliance costs DEC incurs to utilize and monetize the credits.8

        NCEMC’s PTC benefit will be allocated using a demand allocation factor. Because the
actual value of PTCs cannot be determined until after the applicable tax year, Duke will provide
NCEMC with estimated monthly PTC credits followed by an annual true-up, including interest on
any resulting refund or surcharge.

        In the coming weeks, DEC and DEP anticipate filing revisions to their existing wholesale
power contracts to incorporate this refund mechanism for IRA tax credits (as well as other
proposed changes) (“DEC/DEP Amended Agreement Filing”). Should the Commission’s decision
in the DEC/DEP Amended Agreement Filing proceeding impact or alter the proposed tax credit
refund mechanism in this Agreement, Section 6.7 of the Agreement provides that DEC may
modify such provision(s) to the extent necessary to conform to the requirements of FERC’s order.

       D.      Other Provisions

       Article 1 contains the definitions used in the Agreement.

7

8

       expenses associated with obtaining and monetizing the tax credits, incremental prevailing wage costs to
       comply with the IRA, and the incremental costs to track and manage compliance with these and other IRA
       requirements.
 Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary
October 28, 2026
Page 5



       Article 3 establishes additional conditions precedent for the Parties’ obligations under the
Agreement to commence. These include, inter alia (i) the requirement that the Commission has
issued an order accepting or approving the Agreement without condition, or on conditions
acceptable to DEC; (ii) NCEMC has arranged for transmission service such that NCEMC can
accept delivery of the NCEMC Large Load 1 Metered Load under the Agreement; and (iii)
consummation and effectiveness of the Internal Reorganization.

       Article 5 gives NCEMC the right to implement and operate certain energy efficiency
programs but prohibits NCEMC from implementing or operating any DSM Programs or Time of
Use Rates. Article 5 also provides that NCEMC may purchase power from qualifying facilities
under the Public Utilities Regulatory Policies Act,9 but that any capacity and energy purchased
from a qualifying facility may not be used to reduce the Monthly Billing Demand under the
Agreement.

        Article 7 requires DEC to make all necessary arrangements and pay all costs to deliver
energy to the NCEMC Large Load 1 Delivery Points. NCEMC is in turn responsible for making
and paying for all contractual arrangements with the Transmission Provider that are necessary for
the transmission of energy to the NCEMC Large Load 1 Delivery Points under the Agreement.

       Article 8 establishes an Operating Committee to resolve operational issues that arise.

        Article 9 establishes the process for modifying the Agreement. Under Section 9.1.1, either
Party may request FERC authorization to modify the Agreement – except as provided for in
Section 9.1.3 – under the “just and reasonable” standard of review pursuant to FPA Section 205
rather than the higher “public interest” standard as set forth in Morgan Stanley Capital Group, Inc.
v. Public Utility District No. 1 of Snohomish County, 554 U.S. 527 (2008). Under Section 9.1.2,
if any third party, or FERC acting sua sponte, seeks to modify the Agreement, the standard of
review will be the “public interest” standard. Pursuant to Section 9.1.3, DEC and NCEMC agree
that the ROE is fixed at eleven percent (11%) and that the proxy capital structure is forty-five
percent (45%) long term debt and fifty-five percent (55%) common equity, and that the standard
of review for any such modification to the ROE or the proxy capital structure will be the “public
interest” standard. Finally, Section 9.2 provides additional instruction regarding the process for
amendment or modification of terms under the Agreement.

        Articles 10 and 11 contain the Agreement’s billing and dispute resolution provisions,
respectively.

       Article 12 provides for credit and collateral requirements, including notice and
Performance Assurance obligations under certain scenarios.

       Article 13 contains additional terms and conditions, such as default, force majeure and
notice provisions commonly included in agreements of this nature. Article 13.6.6 provides that

9

 Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary
October 28, 2026
Page 6



certain suspensions of NCEMC’s acceptance or receipt of the NCEMC Large Load 1 Load will
not, by themselves, constitute an Event of Default, including a non-bankruptcy SREMC retail-
service suspension lasting up to 100 days and a qualifying bankruptcy-related suspension under
Section 2.5, so long as NCEMC otherwise performs its obligations under the Agreement.

III.   REQUESTS FOR WAIVER

         DEC respectfully requests waiver of any of the Commission’s regulations that otherwise
would require DEC to submit cost information, including the requirement to submit cost of service
statements and other data set forth in 18 C.F.R. § 35.13. The Agreement is based on a cost-based
formula. The Commission routinely grants waiver of the regulations to applicants filing formula
rates because, unlike traditional stated rates, formula rates do not depend upon cost of service
statements.10 DEC also requests waiver of any other applicable requirement of 18 C.F.R. Part 35
that is found not to be completely satisfied by this filing. This is the same approach that DEC has
used in filing prior agreements that contained substantially the same formula rate, which the
Commission has found acceptable.

IV.    CORRESPONDENCE

       Correspondence regarding this filing should be sent to the following individual, who should

                      POWER PURCHASE AGREEMENT
                              BETWEEN
                     DUKE ENERGY CAROLINAS, LLC
                                AND
           NORTH CAROLINA ELECTRIC MEMBERSHIP CORPORATION

        THIS POWER PURCHASE AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”), dated as of October 19,
2026 (the “Execution Date”), is entered into by and between Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC, a
limited liability company organized and existing under the laws of North Carolina, together with
any permitted successor or assignee (“Duke”), and North Carolina Electric Membership
Corporation, a North Carolina electric membership corporation, with its principal offices located
at 3400 Sumner Boulevard, Raleigh, North Carolina 27616 (“Buyer” or “NCEMC”). Hereinafter,
Duke and Buyer are sometimes also referred to individually as a “Party” or collectively as the
“Parties.”

                                     WITNESSETH

        WHEREAS, Duke is engaged in the business of generating, transmitting, and distributing
electric capacity and energy in portions of the states of North Carolina and South Carolina, and
provides electric service to retail and wholesale customers; and

       WHEREAS, Buyer is engaged in the business of generating, transmitting and providing to
its members on a wholesale basis electric power in the State of North Carolina; and

       WHEREAS, Buyer has entered and may hereafter enter into agreements to supply electric
capacity and energy to its member, South River Electric Membership Corporation (“SREMC” or
“Member”), to which Buyer is required to supply electric capacity and energy to SREMC, and
SREMC will use such electric capacity and energy to provide retail electric service; and

        WHEREAS, Buyer has a need for electric capacity and energy which it will sell to SREMC
to enable SREMC to serve the load associated with NCEMC Large Load 1 through a new
substation adjacent to the NCEMC Large Load 1 facility (the “NCEMC Large Load 1
Substation”), and Buyer has determined that it is willing to purchase electric capacity and energy
from Duke for the duration of, and subject to the terms of, this Agreement; and

       WHEREAS, Duke is willing to sell and deliver to Buyer electric capacity and energy for
the duration of, and subject to the terms of, this Agreement.

       NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the promises and the mutual representations,
warranties and covenants set forth in this Agreement, and for other good and valuable
consideration, the receipt and adequacy of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties, each
intending to be legally bound, hereby agree as follows:




                                                4
                                       Article 1 - Definitions

1.1    Definitions.

       Defined terms in this Agreement are capitalized. The defined terms used in this Agreement
have the following meanings:

       “Added-Back Demand” is defined in Section 6.2.2.

        “Affiliate” means, with respect to any person, any other person directly or indirectly
controlling or controlled by, or under direct or indirect common control with, such person. For
purposes of this definition, “control” when used with respect to any person means the power to
direct the management and policies of such person, directly or indirectly, whether through the
ownership of voting securities, by contract or otherwise, and the terms “controlling” and
“controlled” have meanings correlative to the foregoing.

       “Agreement” has the meaning set forth in the Preamble.

        “Ancillary Services” means any and all ancillary services provided by the Transmission
Provider in connection with any Transmission Service arranged by Buyer for the delivery of
electric energy provided under this Agreement from the NCEMC Large Load 1 Delivery Points.

       “Ancillary Services Credit” has the meaning set forth in Section 6.3.1.1.

                        Article 4 - Sale of Electric Capacity and Energy

4.1    Sale and Delivery of Electric Capacity and Energy. During the period beginning on the
Commencement Date, and continuing during each Hour throughout the Term, subject to the terms
and conditions of this Agreement, Duke shall sell and deliver to Buyer the electric capacity and
energy at the NCEMC Large Load 1 Delivery Points that are serving the NCEMC Large Load 1
Native Load. Buyer shall purchase and receive such electric capacity and energy pursuant to the
terms of this Agreement at the NCEMC Large Load 1 Delivery Points. All NCEMC Large Load
1 Native Load is within Duke’s Balancing Authority Area or otherwise connected to the Duke
Transmission System, either directly or indirectly, shall be served at the NCEMC Large Load 1
Delivery Points. Duke shall be entitled to supply the electric capacity and energy provided under
this Agreement from any generating units to which Duke is entitled by ownership, contract or
otherwise to the output.

              4.1.1 NCEMC Large Load 1 Load. The “NCEMC Large Load 1 Load” for each
      Hour, shall be the NCEMC Large Load 1 Metered Load. The only use Buyer may make of
      energy and capacity purchased under this Agreement is service of the NCEMC Large Load
      1 Load. Buyer may not use any other electrical capacity and energy resources of any kind
      to serve the NCEMC Large Load 1 Load at any time during the Term, with the exception
      of Emergency Generating Resources subject to the conditions set forth in Section 4.3.

4.2    Buyer Use of Permitted Additional Resources. Buyer shall not operate Permitted
Additional Resources to serve any NCEMC Large Load 1 Native Load. Any use by Buyer,
Member or Member’s end-use consumers, in each case, of Permitted Additional Resources shall
be Added-Back Demand in accordance with Section 6.2.2.

4.3     Emergency Generating Resources. Buyer or its end-use customer shall have the right to
operate Emergency Generating Resources. An Emergency Generating Resource may be used
solely during an Emergency Condition. The use of an Emergency Generating Resource during
periods when an Emergency Condition does not exist and which reduces the Monthly Coincident
Peak Hour shall constitute Added-Back Demand in accordance with Section 6.2.2.

4.4      Firmness of Service. Duke shall supply and deliver capacity and energy under this
Agreement in a manner that is as firm as, and otherwise comparable with, the manner in which
Duke supplies Duke’s Native Load. Duke shall not curtail the sale and delivery of capacity and
energy to Buyer under this Agreement in order to enable Duke to take advantage of economic
opportunities. In any curtailment of service under this Agreement for any reason, including
implementing transmission curtailments and generation deficits, Duke shall make no adverse
distinction between Duke’s Native Load and Duke’s obligations to sell and deliver capacity and
energy under this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, Duke has entered into this Agreement
in its role as power supplier; neither Duke Transmission nor any other Transmission Provider is a
party to this Agreement. Any curtailments of service, should they occur, will be implemented
pursuant to the terms for non-discriminatory treatment under the Transmission Provider’s OATT.
Duke does not purport to bind the Transmission Provider, or in any way modify the terms of the
OATT or any service agreement under the OATT, by operation of this Agreement.

4.7     Failure to Deliver or Receive Energy. In any Hour, in the event that (i) Duke fails to meet
its obligation under Section 4.1 to sell and deliver energy to satisfy the NCEMC Large Load 1
Load, or (ii) Buyer fails to meet its obligation under Section 4.1 to purchase and receive such
energy to meet the NCEMC Large Load 1 Load, it is expressly acknowledged that the other Party’s

               4.7.1 Duke Failure. For any Hour in which Duke fails to deliver the NCEMC
      Large Load 1 Load and such failure is not excused under the terms of this Agreement, or by
      Buyer’s failure to receive such energy, then Duke shall reduce its Monthly bill to Buyer for
      the Month in which such failure occurred by an amount for such deficiency equal to the
      positive difference, if any, obtained by subtracting the Shortfall Price for such Hour from
      the Replacement Price for such Hour. The Invoice for such Month shall include a written
      statement explaining in reasonable detail the calculation of such amount. “Shortfall Price”
      shall be equal to the product of the NCEMC Large Load 1 Load that Duke failed to deliver
      as described in this Section 4.7.1 and the System Average Energy Rate. “Replacement
      Price” means the price, including any payments for capacity, at which Buyer, using
      Commercially Reasonable Efforts, purchases a replacement for the amount of energy not
      delivered by Duke, plus (i) any costs reasonably incurred by Buyer in purchasing such
      replacement energy and (ii) any transmission charges reasonably incurred by Buyer to the
      Delivery Point, or, at Buyer’s option, the market price at the Delivery Point for such energy
      not delivered as determined by Buyer using Commercially Reasonable Efforts; provided,
      however, in no event shall such price include any penalties or ratcheted demand charges
      incurred in connection with deliveries of replacement energy, nor shall Buyer be required
      to utilize or change its utilization of its owned or controlled assets or market positions to
      minimize Duke’s liability hereunder. Buyer shall remain obligated to pay the Monthly
      Demand Charge for such Month calculated in accordance with Section 6.3.

the purpose of avoiding or reducing the Monthly Coincident Peak Hour.

5.2     PURPA Qualifying Facilities. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement,
Buyer may acquire capacity and energy from one or more generating facilities that qualify as
qualifying facilities under PURPA, to the extent Buyer is legally entitled to purchase such capacity
and energy under PURPA and applicable law. The capacity and energy associated with any such
qualifying facility shall not reduce the Monthly Billing Demand under this Agreement. Instead,
for purposes of determining Buyer's obligations hereunder, the capacity and energy delivered from
such qualifying facility shall be added back to the Monthly Billing Demand for the month in which
such use is billed as if such qualifying facility had not supplied such capacity and energy. Duke
shall purchase from Buyer the capacity and energy generated by such qualifying facility and
delivered in accordance with applicable law and tariff provisions and shall compensate Buyer for
such capacity and energy at the applicable Avoided Cost Rate. For the avoidance of doubt, Buyer


                                                 27
 shall not be entitled to any reduction in its capacity, demand, or energy payment obligations under
this Agreement as a result of the operation of any such qualifying facility.

Article 6 – Capacity, Energy, CCR Charges and CPRE Costs, and IRA Tax Credit Benefits

6.1     General. Buyer shall pay to Duke the Monthly Demand Charge set forth in Section 6.3,
the Monthly Energy Charge set forth in Section 6.4, and the Monthly Charge for Buyer’s CCR
Costs set forth in Section 6.5, and Duke shall credit to Buyer the Monthly Credit for Buyer’s IRA
PTC benefit set forth in Section 6.7, as trued-up in in accordance with Section 6.9. It is intended
that these charges shall exclude any amounts described in Sections 6.5.1 and 6.5.2 (“Excluded
Costs”). If any of the cost items set forth in Exhibits I, II, III, and IV contain any Excluded Costs,
then such costs shall be excluded when calculating charges under this Agreement.

6.2    Monthly Billing Demand.

              6.2.1 Determination of Monthly Billing Demand. “Monthly Billing Demand”
      for a Month shall equal the NCEMC Large Load 1 Metered Load (in kW) at the Monthly
      Coincident Peak Hour. The Added-Back Demand and any other adjustments contemplated
      under this Agreement will be applied to the Monthly Billing Demand during the annual true-
      up as set forth in Section 6.10.

              6.2.2 Added-Back Demand. Any use by Buyer, Member or Member’s end-use
      consumers, in each case, of any resources, including Permitted Additional Resources, to
      reduce Monthly Billing Demand, shall be added back (in MW), the “Added-Back
      Demand”, to the Monthly Billing Demand for the purpose of calculating the Monthly
      Billing Demand for the month in which such use is billed.

6.3     Monthly Demand Charge. The “Monthly Demand Charge” for a Month shall be equal
to the product of (i) the Monthly Billing Demand for the Month (kW) and (ii) the Monthly Demand
Rate ($/kW-Month), minus (iii) the Ancillary Services Credit.

              6.3.1 Monthly Demand Rate. The Demand Rate for each Year shall be calculated
      in accordance with the Rate Formula set forth in Exhibit I. The “Monthly Demand Rate”
      shall initially be calculated based on estimated data, and shall be subject to true-up as set
      forth in Section 6.9.

              6.3.1.1 Ancillary Services Credit. Buyer’s “Ancillary Services Credit” for a
              Month shall be equal to the sum of the charges paid or reimbursed to Duke by Buyer
              to Duke Transmission relating to service provided with respect to energy deliveries
              from Duke to Buyer (excluding any energy from Partial Requirements Resources)
              under this Agreement under Duke Transmission’s OATT for Regulation and
              Frequency Response Service (OATT Schedule 3), Operating Reserve – Spinning
              Reserve Service (OATT Schedule 5) and Operating Reserve – Supplemental
              Reserve Service (OATT Schedule 6) for the Month.

6.4    Monthly Energy Charge. The “Monthly Energy Charge” for a Month shall be equal to
the product of (i) the quantity of energy delivered for the Month (in kWh) and (ii) the System
Average Energy Rate calculated in accordance with the Rate Formula set forth in Exhibit II. The
                                                 28
 System Average Energy Rate shall initially be calculated based on estimated data and shall be
subject to true-up as set forth in Section 6.9.

             6.4.1 Beneficial Reuse Costs. Duke shall include Beneficial Reuse Costs that are
      recorded in FERC Account No. 501 in the System Average Energy Rate determined in
      accordance with Exhibit II.

6.5     Charges for CCR Costs. The Charge for Buyer’s CCR Costs for each year shall be
calculated in accordance with Exhibit III subject to the Excluded Costs set forth in Section 6.5.1.

              6.5.1 Exclusions from Buyer’s CCR Costs. The Parties agree that Buyer shall not
      be responsible for paying, Duke shall not recover from Buyer, and Buyer’s CCR Costs shall
      not include:

              6.5.1.1 Payments ordered in a final, non-appealable order, agreed upon in a final,
              non-appealable settlement, or sought by any third party and which Duke by a final,
              non-appealable settlement expressly agrees to assume or pay for third-party personal
              injury or property damage caused or alleged to have been caused by either: (a) CCR
              Compliance Activities, or (b) the release or threatened release to the environment of
              any of Duke CCR under 42 U.S.C. § 9607 or 9613 (or any substantively similar state
              law), whether such payment liability for either (a) or (b) results from litigation or
              settlement;

              6.5.1.2 Costs associated with excavation of impoundments that are eligible for
              low-risk classification by the Department of Environmental Quality under CAMA,
              but that do not receive the low-risk classification because Duke, its contractors
              and/or agents fail to provide permanent replacement water supplies or fails to correct
              deficiencies identified in any dam safety order issued by the Environmental
              Management Commission; and

              6.5.1.3 Additional costs and/or damages, such as fines, penalties, settlements, or
              judgments, incurred or sought while Duke, its contractors and/or agents are
              performing, or after Duke, its contractors and/or agents have completed all or a
              portion of its CCR Compliance Activities in accordance with prudent utility
              practices and in a non-negligent manner at a particular impoundment or landfill and
              Buyer has paid for its share of the corresponding CCR Costs as set forth herein, and
              which Duke expressly agrees to pay either voluntarily or in a final non-appealable
              settlement agreement, or for which Duke is found liable in a final non-appealable
              order.

             6.5.2 Post-CCR Compliance Activities Costs. After Duke, its contractors and/or
      agents have performed CCR Compliance Activities at a particular impoundment or landfill,
      Buyer shall no longer be liable for any CCR Costs associated with CCR at or from such
      impoundment or landfill. Duke shall not recover from Buyer and Duke shall hold Buyer
      harmless from any costs associated with CCR that has been relocated for storage and/or
      otherwise remediated as part of CCR Compliance Activities. However, Buyer shall pay for
      the ongoing operations, maintenance, and monitoring costs for CCR remediated by Duke,

                                                29
       its contractors and/or agents, and which is located at an impoundment or landfill owned by
      Duke.

              6.5.3 Limitations on Disallowances. Except as set forth in Sections 6.5.1 and 6.5.2,
      Buyer agrees that it shall not receive, and Buyer hereby irrevocably waives any right to
      receive or seek to receive, any cost treatment, rate methodology, disallowance, and/or the
      benefit of any CCR Costs that Duke is prohibited from recovering and/or are not approved
      or accepted for recovery for any reason by the NCUC, PSCSC, and/or FERC; provided
      however, Duke shall not re-allocate for recovery from Buyer the portion of such CCR Costs
      that Duke has been prohibited from recovering and does not recover from any other retail
      or wholesale customer as a result of such rulings by the NCUC, PSCSC, and/or FERC.

6.6     Charges for CPRE Costs. Buyer agrees that Duke shall be entitled to permitted recovery
of the CPRE Costs as outlined in the Rate Formulas.

6.7     IRA Tax Credit Benefits. Duke shall use Commercially Reasonable Efforts to apply any
earned IRA Tax Credits to reduce Duke’s (or its Affiliates’) tax liability for a particular tax year.
Should the IRA Tax Credits exceed Duke’s tax liability for such tax year, Duke shall use
Commercially Reasonable Efforts to sell or transfer any remaining IRA Tax Credits to a third
party. Duke may, in its sole discretion, sell or transfer such earned IRA Tax Credits at a discounted
rate in any Year, including one (1) or more Years following the particular tax year in which such
credits are earned. In the Year after such IRA Tax Credits are monetized, Duke shall pay to Buyer
an amount equal to (i) with respect to earned and monetized IRA PTCs, the Monthly Credit for
Buyer’s IRA PTC Benefit and (ii) with respect to earned and monetized IRA ITCs, an amount for
Buyer’s IRA ITC Benefit, which shall be included in the Rate Formulas. Calculations of Buyer’s
IRA PTC Benefit for any applicable tax year shall be provided to Buyer in accordance with Section
6.9 and Exhibit IV. Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, if FERC, in
accepting, approving, or permitting Duke’s forthcoming filing proposing implementation of
Buyer’s IRA PTC Benefit and Buyer’s IRA ITC Benefit, requires modification of any provision
of this Agreement relating to the calculation of Buyer’s IRA PTC Benefit or Buyer’s IRA ITC
Benefit, or the allocation, treatment, or recovery thereof, Duke may modify such provision(s) to
the extent necessary to conform to the requirements of FERC’s order solely to the extent required
by FERC in such order.

6.8    Transmission and Generator Step-Up Transformer Losses.

              6.8.1 General. For the purpose of calculating energy delivered and demand
      hereunder, quantities shall be at the generator level, i.e., grossed up for all transmission
      losses and generator step-up transformer losses which are incurred between the point of
      generation and the point of interconnection of the Transmission System and Buyer’s
      distribution system. The loss factor used in such calculations shall be the sum of (i) the
      Real Power Loss factor in the DEC Zone as stated in the Transmission Provider’s OATT,
      as it may be amended from time to time, and (ii) the GSU Loss Factor as determined under
      Section 6.8.2.

            6.8.2 GSU Loss Factor. After each Year, Duke shall calculate the applicable GSU
      Loss Factor in accordance with the Attachment W Methodology for Calculation of Real

                                                 30
       Power Loss Factor in Duke’s Open Access Transmission Tariff. By April 1 of the Year
      immediately succeeding the twelve (12)-Month loss factor calculation period, Duke shall
      give notice to Buyer stating the revised GSU Loss Factor (the “Revised GSU Loss Factor”)
      along with supporting calculations and documentation in sufficient detail to enable Buyer
      to verify the accuracy of the Revised GSU Loss Factor. The Revised GSU Loss Factor shall
      be effective June 1st following the giving of such notice. The Revised GSU Loss Factor
      shall be subject to Buyer’s audit rights as set forth in Section 10.4.

6.9    Annual True-Up.

             6.9.1 Estimated Charges. Duke shall provide Buyer its estimated Monthly
      Demand Rate, estimated System Average Energy Rate, estimated Monthly Charge for
      Buyer’s CCR Costs, and the estimated Monthly Credit for Buyer’s IRA PTC Benefit for the
      succeeding Year by December 1st of the current Year, each of which will be subject to
      annual true-up as set forth in this Section 6.9.

              6.9.2 Annual True-Up. Following the end of each Year, Duke shall reconcile the
      estimated charges and credits billed with the actual charges and credits for that Year. The
      net difference between the estimated amounts and the actual amounts shall be the “Annual
      True-Up Amount”. The Monthly Demand Rate, the Monthly Billing Demand, the Ancillary
      Services Credits, the System Average Energy Rate, the Monthly Charge for Buyer’s CCR
      Costs, and the Monthly Credit for Buyer’s IRA PTC Benefit each shall be trued-up annually
      after actual data for such Year becomes available. Duke shall provide the preliminary true-
      up data to Buyer no later than June 15 following the Year in which the Partial Requirements
      Service was provided, and shall provide the actual true-up data to Buyer on or about July 1
      following such Year.

              6.9.3 True-Up of Monthly Charge for Buyer’s CCR Costs. CCR Disallowances
      that are ordered or determined under an applicable Law that are related to a Year in which
      the annual true-up for the System Average Energy Rate and/or the Monthly Charge for
      Buyer’s CCR Costs has already occurred shall be adjusted in accordance with Section IV.A
      of Exhibit III. Adjustments for such additional CCR Disallowances shall survive
      termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 13.10.

6.10 Payment of Annual True-Up Amount. The Annual True-Up Amount shall be paid or
credited along with the Monthly statement in accordance with the billing and payment provisions
in Article 10. To the extent that the Buyer selects the lump sum payment option as set forth in
Section 6.11.1, such lump sum payment shall be included in the June statement, which will be
issued during the first week of July, and it will be payable on July 20th.

             6.10.1 Refund. If the Annual True-Up Amount reflects that estimated charges
      exceeded actual charges, then Duke shall refund the difference to Buyer as a lump sum.

             6.10.2 Surcharge. If the Annual True-Up Amount reflects that actual charges
      exceeded estimated charges, then Buyer shall pay the difference to Duke as a lump sum.

             6.10.3 Interest. The Annual True-Up Amount shall include interest payable by
      Buyer or Duke, as applicable, on any refunds or surcharges calculated at the Interest Rate
                                              31
        from the date on which the overpayment or underpayment was made to the date on which
       the refund or surcharge is due and paid.

6.11   Installment Payment Option.

              6.11.1 Buyer’s Election. Following delivery of the actual true-up data pursuant to
       Section 6.9, Buyer may elect to pay the Annual True-Up Amount surcharge or receive the
       Annual True-Up Amount refund (as applicable), either in a lump sum or in twelve (12)
       equal Monthly installments payments (“Installment Payment Option”). In the event
       Buyer desires to elect the Installment Payment Option, Buyer must notify Duke, in writing,
       within ten (10) Business Days of receiving the actual true-up data under Section 6.9. If
       Buyer does not timely notify Duke of such election, Buyer shall be deemed to have elected
       lump sum payments or credits, as applicable, in accordance with Section 6.10.

               6.11.2 Limitations. The Installment Payment Option is subject to the following
       limitations:

              6.11.2.1       The twelve (12) Monthly installments will be made in equal
              amounts for the ensuing twelve (12)-Month period, which begins with the June bill
              each Year, shall not extend beyond the May bill of the following Year;

              6.11.2.2        The (12) Monthly installment amounts shall include interest payable
              at the Interest Rate from the date on which the overpayment or underpayment was
              made to the date on which the refund or surcharge is due and paid; provided,
              however, Duke shall only pay interest on a refund under the lump sum payment or
              the Installment Payment Option until July 20th of each Year, which is the due date
              for the lump sum payment, even if Buyer chooses to receive a refund under the
              Installment Payment Option;

              6.11.2.3        Unless otherwise agreed upon by Duke in writing in its sole
              discretion, the amount of the true-up that Buyer may pay back to Duke over a
              maximum twelve-Month period is limited to an amount not to exceed five percent
              (5%) of the Buyer’s total annual billings, and the Buyer must pay the excess (> five
              percent (5%) of total annual billed amounts) in a lump sum payment in the June
              bill; and

              6.11.2.4      Duke has the right to revoke the Installment Payment Option and
              require a lump sum payment for the true-up if the Buyer does not maintain timely
              payment history.

                   Article 7 - Transmission, Energy Imbalance, and RTO

7.1     Transmission Arrangements. Duke shall be responsible for making all arrangements
necessary and paying for all costs incurred under contractual arrangements necessary to transmit
the electric energy provided hereunder to the NCEMC Large Load 1 Delivery Points. Buyer shall
be responsible for making and paying for all contractual arrangements with the Transmission
Provider necessary for the transmission of the electric energy provided hereunder from the
NCEMC Large Load 1 Delivery Points. This Agreement does not obligate Duke to provide, pay
                                               32
 for, or make arrangements for, any Transmission Services. Duke shall have no responsibility for
any costs incurred in connection with the construction of any transmission and/or distribution
facilities necessary for delivery of energy to NCEMC Large Load 1 Delivery Points.

7.2     Energy Imbalance. Duke shall reimburse Buyer for any Hour in which, as a result of
Duke’s delivery of an amount of energy less than the NCEMC Large Load 1 Load (unless excused
under this Agreement), Energy Imbalance Service charges are incurred by Buyer in accordance
with the Transmission Provider’s OATT. Buyer shall reimburse Duke for any Hour in which, as
a result of Duke’s delivery of an amount of energy in excess of the NCEMC Large Load 1 Load,
Energy Imbalance Service compensation is provided to Buyer in accordance with the Transmission
Provider’s OATT.

7.3     Regional Transmission Organization. If an ISO, RTO, independent transmission company
or other future organization, agency or authority is approved by FERC to serve as the Transmission
Provider in replacement of Duke Transmission, then Duke and Buyer will reasonably cooperate to
make or enter into replacement arrangements with such entity to the extent required in connection
with the implementation of this Agreement. The Parties expressly acknowledge and agree that
neither the implementation of an ISO, RTO, independent transmission company or other future
organization, agency or authority that has been approved by FERC to serve as the Transmission
Provider nor the failure of the Parties to enter into the arrangements contemplated under this
Section 7.3 shall relieve either Party of any obligations under this Agreement.

              7.3.1 Cost Responsibility. Buyer expressly acknowledges and agrees that nothing
      herein shall be construed to in any way relieve Buyer of, or impose upon Duke, the
      responsibility for any fees, costs, or charges (including congestion costs, transmission
      losses, or the costs or charges to secure financial transmission rights or the equivalent
      thereof) that may be imposed on Buyer by an ISO, RTO, independent transmission company
      or other future organization, agency or authority that has been approved by FERC to serve
      as the Transmission Provider in connection with Transmission Service or Ancillary
      Services. The Parties expressly acknowledge and agree that neither Party shall have any
      right or interest in any financial transmission rights, congestion revenue rights, or other
      financial rights to firm transmission as may be defined or authorized by regulatory authority
      that are allocated to, assigned to, transferred to or acquired by the other Party.

      Transmission offers transmission service on its system in a manner intended to comply with
      FERC policies and requirements relating to the provision of open-access transmission
      service. Buyer expressly recognizes that for purposes hereof Duke Transmission shall be
      deemed to be a separate entity and separate contracting party from Duke. Buyer
      acknowledges that Duke, acting in its merchant capacity function hereunder, has no
      responsibility for or control over Duke Transmission, and is not liable for any breach of
      agreement or duty by Duke Transmission or any other Transmission Provider. The Parties
      acknowledge and agree that all arrangements for transmission shall be separate and free-
      standing contracts and that the terms hereof are not binding upon Duke Transmission.

       Notwithstanding any other provision in this Agreement, nothing in any agreement between

                                Article 8 - Operating Committee

Committee, plus any alternate, by written notice delivered in accordance with Section 13.21 within

coordination and interaction between the Parties with respect to the performance of the duties and

protocols and procedures therefor. The Operating Committee shall not, however, have any
authority to modify or otherwise alter the Parties’ rights and obligations under this Agreement.

                                Article 10 - Billing and Payment

10.1 Billing Period. Unless otherwise specifically provided in this Agreement or agreed upon
by the Parties in writing, the Month shall be the standard period for determining all billings and
payments under this Agreement.

       to Buyer a statement setting forth for the Billing Period (i) the sum of the electric energy
       delivered for all Hours during that Billing Period, and (ii) Duke’s calculation of any amounts
       due from Buyer under this Agreement for the Billing Period (“Billing Statement”).
       Notwithstanding the foregoing, Duke’s failure to render a statement as set forth above shall
       not relieve Buyer from its obligation to make payment when such statement is rendered,
       provided such statement is rendered within twelve (12) Months after the end of the Billing
       Period provided, however, such twelve (12) Month limitation shall not apply to billing

                                                 35
        credits Duke is obligated to provide Buyer as a result of CCR Insurance Proceeds in
       accordance with Section IV of Exhibit III. Duke may adjust any statement for arithmetic or
       computational error within twelve (12) Months after the date of the original statement.

       will be made on an estimated basis. In addition, the Parties agree that after-the-fact
       adjustments to amounts owed may be made by Duke in order to reflect correctly the amounts

       may be withheld pursuant to Section 10.3, not paid by the due date shall be deemed
       delinquent and shall accrue interest at the Interest Rate, such interest to be calculated from

               perform any obligation to, Buyer shall not excuse Buyer from any obligation to pay
               Duke, or perform any other obligation imposed upon Buyer under this Agreement.

(including the Annual True-Up Invoice) rendered under this Agreement. As provided in
Section 11.2 and subject to the process below, Buyer may dispute anything concerning any

resolution of such Dispute.

(18) months following delivery of the Annual True-Up Invoice with respect to such period of
service, Buyer shall have forever and irrevocably waived (without any reservation of rights) any
right to make any claims with respect to anything about such Invoice. If Buyer timely delivers a

 Billing Dispute Notice within such eighteen (18) Month period, each Party will work in good faith

12.1 Material Adverse Change. Each of the Parties shall be deemed to have experienced a
material adverse change (“MAC”) if it is no longer Creditworthy.



                                                  38
 12.2 Notice. Each Party shall provide the other Party written notice within two (2) Business
Days of the occurrence of a MAC affecting the notifying Party or of the occurrence of any event
that may reasonably cause a MAC.

12.3 Performance Assurance. To protect either Party against potential default of payment or
performance, any Party that experiences a MAC shall post as Performance Assurance in an amount
equal to the highest two (2) Months of Duke’s billings under this Agreement for the previous
twelve (12) Months. Such Performance Assurance shall be provided by the Party experiencing
the MAC in a cash deposit or letters of credit from a financial institution reasonably acceptable to
the Party not experiencing the MAC within five (5) Business Days after the date on which the
MAC occurs. Any letter of credit shall be in a form satisfactory to the Party not experiencing the
MAC in its sole commercially reasonable discretion. If the Performance Assurance is in the form
of a letter of credit, the Party experiencing the MAC (“the posting Party”) will ensure that the letter
of credit remains in full force, outstanding and in the required amount through the term of this
Agreement. The letter of credit shall provide that if (i) the letter of credit is within thirty (30) days of
expiration and (ii) the posting Party has failed to renew or replace the letter of credit pursuant to the
terms of this section, then the Party not experiencing the MAC (“the other Party”) may draw and
retain the full amount of the letter of credit to be held as security for the posting Party’s obligations
under this Agreement. If at any time the rating of the issuer of the letter of credit falls below A- with
S&P or A3 with Moody’s and the posting Party fails to replace the letter of credit with Performance
Assurance in accordance with this Agreement within five (5) Business Days, then the other Party
shall be entitled to draw and retain the full amount of the letter of credit.

        If the posting Party has provided a letter of credit as Performance Assurance and subsequently
desires to replace it with a cash deposit, the posting Party, upon written notice to the other Party, may
substitute the Performance Assurance with a cash deposit, or if the posting Party has provided a cash
deposit and subsequently desires to replace it with a letter of credit, the posting Party, upon written
notice to the other Party, may substitute the Performance Assurance with a letter of credit conforming
to the requirements of this Agreement. If the posting Party elects to provide such substitute
Performance Assurance, the other Party will return to the posting Party (or to the Issuing Bank if a
letter of credit) the Performance Assurance previously provided upon receipt of the replacement
Performance Assurance.

12.4 Security Interest in Cash Deposit. To the extent that a posting Party delivers Performance
Assurance hereunder in the form of a cash deposit, the posting Party hereby grants to the other
Party a present and continuing security interest in, and lien on (and right of netting and set-off
against), and assignment of, such Performance Assurance, including, without limitation, cash
collateral and cash equivalent collateral and any and all proceeds resulting therefrom or the
liquidation thereof, whether now or hereafter held by, on behalf of, or for the benefit of, the other
Party; and agrees to take such action as the other Party reasonably requires to perfect the other
Party’s first-priority security interest in, and lien on (and right of netting and set-off against), such
Performance Assurance and any and all proceeds resulting therefrom or from the liquidation
thereof.

12.5 Interest on Cash Used as Collateral. If cash collateral is posted, the Party holding the cash
collateral shall pay interest to the posting Party at the Federal Funds Effective Rate. The Federal
Funds Effective Rate is the rate for that day opposite the caption “Federal Funds (Effective)” as

                                                    39
 set forth in the weekly statistical release designated as H.15(519), or any successor publication
published by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. The posting Party shall
invoice the other Party for interest accrued during the previous Month and the other Party shall
pay such amount within ten (10) days of receipt of such invoice.

12.6 Continuing Nature of Collateral Requirement. The posting Party must continue to post the
collateral until the MAC is cured. The other Party shall have the right to draw upon, use, and
dispose of all collateral that is posted under Section 12.3, if the posting Party fails to fulfill any of
its payment or performance obligations under this Agreement, and such failure shall constitute an
Event of Default. In the event any collateral is drawn upon by the other Party in accordance with
the provisions of this Section 12.6, the posting Party shall within three (3) Business Days fully

      will provide an estimate for only the Duke Formula Rate for Capacity for calendar years six

              13.12.2System Average Energy Rate Information. No later than December 1 of each
      calendar year, Duke shall provide to Buyer the System Average Energy Rate, in $/MWh,
      for use in the next calendar year and a forecast for the next five (5) years. At approximately
      mid-year of the calendar year that service is provided, or at another date mutually agreed to
      by the Parties, the Parties will review the estimated System Average Energy Rate and
      consider if an adjustment to the estimated System Average Energy Rate is desired to more
      closely approximate the expected System Average Energy Rate for the subject year. If the
      Parties agree, Duke will adjust the estimated System Average Energy Rate to the agreed
      upon estimate until such time as the true-up is implemented.

              Duke agrees to perform periodic reviews for the calculation of the System Average
      Energy Rate for the subject calendar year. Duke shall informally communicate, via e-mail
      or telephone, the results of this review to Buyer with a current estimate of calendar year-
      end Energy Charges. In the event that the current estimate does not change by a Material
      Amount, the estimate shall remain the same until such time as the estimate does change by
      a Material Amount. For the purpose of this Agreement, a “Material Amount” shall be an
      amount greater than one percent (1%).

      including, but not limited to expected fuel mix, the hedged fuel amount, hedged fuel prices,

      forecast. For these forecasted rates, the estimated rates will reflect the expected annual
      energy related costs as well as the corresponding annual net generated and purchased MWh

        THIS POWER PURCHASE AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”), dated as of October 19,
2026 (the “Execution Date”), is entered into by and between Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC, a
limited liability company organized and existing under the laws of North Carolina, together with
any permitted successor or assignee (“Duke”), and North Carolina Electric Membership
Corporation, a North Carolina electric membership corporation, with its principal offices located
at 3400 Sumner Boulevard, Raleigh, North Carolina 27616 (“Buyer” or “NCEMC”).
Hereinafter, Duke and Buyer are sometimes also referred to individually as a “Party” or
collectively as the “Parties.”

                                     WITNESSETH

        WHEREAS, Duke is engaged in the business of generating, transmitting, and distributing
electric capacity and energy in portions of the states of North Carolina and South Carolina, and
provides electric service to retail and wholesale customers; and

        WHEREAS, Buyer is engaged in the business of generating, transmitting and providing
to its members on a wholesale basis electric power in the State of North Carolina; and

        WHEREAS, Buyer has entered and may hereafter enter into agreements to supply
electric capacity and energy to its member, South River Electric Membership Corporation
(“SREMC” or “Member”), to which Buyer is required to supply electric capacity and energy to
SREMC, and SREMC will use such electric capacity and energy to provide retail electric
service; and

       WHEREAS, Buyer has a need for electric capacity and energy which it will sell to
SREMC to enable SREMC to serve the load associated with NCEMC Large Load 1 through a
new substation adjacent to the NCEMC Large Load 1 facility (the “NCEMC Large Load 1
Substation”), and Buyer has determined that it is willing to purchase electric capacity and
energy from Duke for the duration of, and subject to the terms of, this Agreement; and

       WHEREAS, Duke is willing to sell and deliver to Buyer electric capacity and energy for
the duration of, and subject to the terms of, this Agreement.

       NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the promises and the mutual representations,
warranties and covenants set forth in this Agreement, and for other good and valuable
consideration, the receipt and adequacy of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties, each
intending to be legally bound, hereby agree as follows:




                                               4
                                     Article 1 - Definitions

1.1    Definitions.

      Defined terms in this Agreement are capitalized.        The defined terms used in this
Agreement have the following meanings:

       “Added-Back Demand” is defined in Section 6.2.2.

        “Affiliate” means, with respect to any person, any other person directly or indirectly
controlling or controlled by, or under direct or indirect common control with, such person. For
purposes of this definition, “control” when used with respect to any person means the power to
direct the management and policies of such person, directly or indirectly, whether through the
ownership of voting securities, by contract or otherwise, and the terms “controlling” and
“controlled” have meanings correlative to the foregoing.

       “Agreement” has the meaning set forth in the Preamble.

        “Ancillary Services” means any and all ancillary services provided by the Transmission

Agreement, and no charges or other amounts shall accrue or be payable under this Agreement

suspension period (as it may be shortened or extended by mutual written agreement), (i) Buyer

                       Article 4 - Sale of Electric Capacity and Energy

Commencement Date, and continuing during each Hour throughout the Term, subject to the
terms and conditions of this Agreement, Duke shall sell and deliver to Buyer the electric capacity
                                              21
 and energy at the NCEMC Large Load 1 Delivery Points that are serving the NCEMC Large
Load 1 Native Load. Buyer shall purchase and receive such electric capacity and energy
pursuant to the terms of this Agreement at the NCEMC Large Load 1 Delivery Points. All
NCEMC Large Load 1 Native Load is within Duke’s Balancing Authority Area or otherwise
connected to the Duke Transmission System, either directly or indirectly, shall be served at the
NCEMC Large Load 1 Delivery Points. Duke shall be entitled to supply the electric capacity
and energy provided under this Agreement from any generating units to which Duke is entitled
by ownership, contract or otherwise to the output.

             4.1.1 NCEMC Large Load 1 Load. The “NCEMC Large Load 1 Load” for
      each Hour, shall be the NCEMC Large Load 1 Metered Load. The only use Buyer may

      Large Load 1 Load. Buyer may not use any other electrical capacity and energy resources
      of any kind to serve the NCEMC Large Load 1 Load at any time during the Term, with the
      exception of Emergency Generating Resources subject to the conditions set forth in
      Section 4.3.

4.2    Buyer Use of Permitted Additional Resources. Buyer shall not operate Permitted
Additional Resources to serve any NCEMC Large Load 1 Native Load. Any use by Buyer,
Member or Member’s end-use consumers, in each case, of Permitted Additional Resources shall

operate Emergency Generating Resources. An Emergency Generating Resource may be used
solely during an Emergency Condition. The use of an Emergency Generating Resource during
periods when an Emergency Condition does not exist and which reduces the Monthly Coincident
Peak Hour shall constitute Added-Back Demand in accordance with Section 6.2.2.

4.4      Firmness of Service. Duke shall supply and deliver capacity and energy under this
Agreement in a manner that is as firm as, and otherwise comparable with, the manner in which
Duke supplies Duke’s Native Load. Duke shall not curtail the sale and delivery of capacity and
energy to Buyer under this Agreement in order to enable Duke to take advantage of economic
opportunities. In any curtailment of service under this Agreement for any reason, including
implementing transmission curtailments and generation deficits, Duke shall make no adverse
distinction between Duke’s Native Load and Duke’s obligations to sell and deliver capacity and
energy under this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, Duke has entered into this Agreement
in its role as power supplier; neither Duke Transmission nor any other Transmission Provider is a
party to this Agreement. Any curtailments of service, should they occur, will be implemented
pursuant to the terms for non-discriminatory treatment under the Transmission Provider’s OATT.

      except for Duke’s failure to comply with the provisions of Section 4.4 or this Section
      4.4.1, Duke shall not be liable to Buyer or Member for damages resulting from any
      interruptions or impairment of service. If and to the extent that Duke, in its role as
      transmission customer under the OATT, is called to exercise discretion in response to a

                                               22
       curtailment instruction from the Transmission Provider, Duke shall not adversely
      distinguish against the supply of NCEMC Large Load 1 Native Load when curtailing
      Duke’s Native Load and reducing its supply of NCEMC Large Load 1 Native Load, or in

4.6     Power Quality. All electric energy provided hereunder at the Delivery Point shall be
three (3) phase, sixty (60) hertz, and at Delivery Point nominal voltages.

4.7    Failure to Deliver or Receive Energy. In any Hour, in the event that (i) Duke fails to
meet its obligation under Section 4.1 to sell and deliver energy to satisfy the NCEMC Large
Load 1 Load, or (ii) Buyer fails to meet its obligation under Section 4.1 to purchase and receive
such energy to meet the NCEMC Large Load 1 Load, it is expressly acknowledged that the other
Party’s exclusive remedy for such failure shall be as set out in Sections 4.7.1 or 4.7.2, as
applicable.

              4.7.1 Duke Failure. For any Hour in which Duke fails to deliver the NCEMC
      Large Load 1 Load and such failure is not excused under the terms of this Agreement, or
      by Buyer’s failure to receive such energy, then Duke shall reduce its Monthly bill to Buyer
      for the Month in which such failure occurred by an amount for such deficiency equal to
      the positive difference, if any, obtained by subtracting the Shortfall Price for such Hour
      from the Replacement Price for such Hour. The Invoice for such Month shall include a
      written statement explaining in reasonable detail the calculation of such amount.
      “Shortfall Price” shall be equal to the product of the NCEMC Large Load 1 Load that
      Duke failed to deliver as described in this Section 4.7.1 and the System Average Energy
      Rate. “Replacement Price” means the price, including any payments for capacity, at
      which Buyer, using Commercially Reasonable Efforts, purchases a replacement for the
      amount of energy not delivered by Duke, plus (i) any costs reasonably incurred by Buyer
      in purchasing such replacement energy and (ii) any transmission charges reasonably
      incurred by Buyer to the Delivery Point, or, at Buyer’s option, the market price at the
      Delivery Point for such energy not delivered as determined by Buyer using Commercially
      Reasonable Efforts; provided, however, in no event shall such price include any penalties
      or ratcheted demand charges incurred in connection with deliveries of replacement energy,
      nor shall Buyer be required to utilize or change its utilization of its owned or controlled
      assets or market positions to minimize Duke’s liability hereunder. Buyer shall remain
      obligated to pay the Monthly Demand Charge for such Month calculated in accordance
      with Section 6.3.

              4.7.2 Buyer Failure. For any Month in which Buyer fails to accept delivery of or
      to receive the NCEMC Large Load 1 Load for one or more Hours for any reason other
      than the occurrence and continuance of (i) an event of Force Majeure, or (ii) a bankruptcy
      transition period as described in Section 2.5, Buyer shall remain obligated to pay the
      Monthly Demand Charge for such Month calculated in accordance with Section 6.3.
