5.1     DSM Programs, Energy Efficiency Programs, and Time of Use Rates. Buyer shall have
the right to implement and operate Energy Efficiency Programs. Buyer shall not have the right
to implement or operate any DSM Programs or Time of Use Rates. Notwithstanding the
foregoing, Buyer or its end-use customer shall have the right to install, replace, upgrade,
maintain, or operate manufacturing equipment, machinery, processes, lighting systems, motors,
drives, controls, or other equipment that improves energy efficiency or production efficiency;
provided, however, that Buyer shall not temporarily shift, suspend, or relocate manufacturing
processes or electric load for the purpose of avoiding or reducing the Monthly Coincident Peak
Hour.

5.2     PURPA Qualifying Facilities. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement,
Buyer may acquire capacity and energy from one or more generating facilities that qualify as
qualifying facilities under PURPA, to the extent Buyer is legally entitled to purchase such
capacity and energy under PURPA and applicable law. The capacity and energy associated with
any such qualifying facility shall not reduce the Monthly Billing Demand under this Agreement.
Instead, for purposes of determining Buyer's obligations hereunder, the capacity and energy
delivered from such qualifying facility shall be added back to the Monthly Billing Demand for
the month in which such use is billed as if such qualifying facility had not supplied such capacity
and energy. Duke shall purchase from Buyer the capacity and energy generated by such
qualifying facility and delivered in accordance with applicable law and tariff provisions and shall
compensate Buyer for such capacity and energy at the applicable Avoided Cost Rate. For the
avoidance of doubt, Buyer shall not be entitled to any reduction in its capacity, demand, or

                                                27
 energy payment obligations under this Agreement as a result of the operation of any such
qualifying facility.

Article 6 – Capacity, Energy, CCR Charges and CPRE Costs, and IRA Tax Credit Benefits

6.1    General. Buyer shall pay to Duke the Monthly Demand Charge set forth in Section 6.3,
the Monthly Energy Charge set forth in Section 6.4, and the Monthly Charge for Buyer’s CCR
Costs set forth in Section 6.5, and Duke shall credit to Buyer the Monthly Credit for Buyer’s
IRA PTC benefit set forth in Section 6.7, as trued-up in in accordance with Section 6.9. It is
intended that these charges shall exclude any amounts described in Sections 6.5.1 and 6.5.2
(“Excluded Costs”). If any of the cost items set forth in Exhibits I, II, III, and IV contain any
Excluded Costs, then such costs shall be excluded when calculating charges under this
Agreement.

6.2    Monthly Billing Demand.

             6.2.1 Determination of Monthly Billing Demand. “Monthly Billing Demand”
      for a Month shall equal the NCEMC Large Load 1 Metered Load (in kW) at the Monthly
      Coincident Peak Hour. The Added-Back Demand and any other adjustments contemplated
      under this Agreement will be applied to the Monthly Billing Demand during the annual
      true-up as set forth in Section 6.10.

              6.2.2 Added-Back Demand. Any use by Buyer, Member or Member’s end-use
      consumers, in each case, of any resources, including Permitted Additional Resources, to
      reduce Monthly Billing Demand, shall be added back (in MW), the “Added-Back
      Demand”, to the Monthly Billing Demand for the purpose of calculating the Monthly
      Billing Demand for the month in which such use is billed.

6.3    Monthly Demand Charge. The “Monthly Demand Charge” for a Month shall be equal
to the product of (i) the Monthly Billing Demand for the Month (kW) and (ii) the Monthly
Demand Rate ($/kW-Month), minus (iii) the Ancillary Services Credit.

              6.3.1 Monthly Demand Rate. The Demand Rate for each Year shall be
      calculated in accordance with the Rate Formula set forth in Exhibit I. The “Monthly
      Demand Rate” shall initially be calculated based on estimated data, and shall be subject
      to true-up as set forth in Section 6.9.

             6.3.1.1 Ancillary Services Credit. Buyer’s “Ancillary Services Credit” for a
             Month shall be equal to the sum of the charges paid or reimbursed to Duke by
             Buyer to Duke Transmission relating to service provided with respect to energy
             deliveries from Duke to Buyer (excluding any energy from Partial Requirements
             Resources) under this Agreement under Duke Transmission’s OATT for
             Regulation and Frequency Response Service (OATT Schedule 3), Operating
             Reserve – Spinning Reserve Service (OATT Schedule 5) and Operating Reserve –
             Supplemental Reserve Service (OATT Schedule 6) for the Month.

6.4    Monthly Energy Charge. The “Monthly Energy Charge” for a Month shall be equal to
the product of (i) the quantity of energy delivered for the Month (in kWh) and (ii) the System
                                               28
 Average Energy Rate calculated in accordance with the Rate Formula set forth in Exhibit II.
The System Average Energy Rate shall initially be calculated based on estimated data and shall
be subject to true-up as set forth in Section 6.9.

             6.4.1 Beneficial Reuse Costs. Duke shall include Beneficial Reuse Costs that are
      recorded in FERC Account No. 501 in the System Average Energy Rate determined in
      accordance with Exhibit II.

6.5     Charges for CCR Costs. The Charge for Buyer’s CCR Costs for each year shall be
calculated in accordance with Exhibit III subject to the Excluded Costs set forth in Section 6.5.1.

              6.5.1 Exclusions from Buyer’s CCR Costs. The Parties agree that Buyer shall
      not be responsible for paying, Duke shall not recover from Buyer, and Buyer’s CCR Costs
      shall not include:

              6.5.1.1 Payments ordered in a final, non-appealable order, agreed upon in a
              final, non-appealable settlement, or sought by any third party and which Duke by a
              final, non-appealable settlement expressly agrees to assume or pay for third-party
              personal injury or property damage caused or alleged to have been caused by
              either: (a) CCR Compliance Activities, or (b) the release or threatened release to
              the environment of any of Duke CCR under 42 U.S.C. § 9607 or 9613 (or any
              substantively similar state law), whether such payment liability for either (a) or (b)
              results from litigation or settlement;

              6.5.1.2 Costs associated with excavation of impoundments that are eligible for
              low-risk classification by the Department of Environmental Quality under CAMA,
              but that do not receive the low-risk classification because Duke, its contractors
              and/or agents fail to provide permanent replacement water supplies or fails to
              correct deficiencies identified in any dam safety order issued by the Environmental
              Management Commission; and

              6.5.1.3 Additional costs and/or damages, such as fines, penalties, settlements, or
              judgments, incurred or sought while Duke, its contractors and/or agents are
              performing, or after Duke, its contractors and/or agents have completed all or a
              portion of its CCR Compliance Activities in accordance with prudent utility
              practices and in a non-negligent manner at a particular impoundment or landfill
              and Buyer has paid for its share of the corresponding CCR Costs as set forth
              herein, and which Duke expressly agrees to pay either voluntarily or in a final non-
              appealable settlement agreement, or for which Duke is found liable in a final non-
              appealable order.

              6.5.2 Post-CCR Compliance Activities Costs. After Duke, its contractors and/or
      agents have performed CCR Compliance Activities at a particular impoundment or
      landfill, Buyer shall no longer be liable for any CCR Costs associated with CCR at or
      from such impoundment or landfill. Duke shall not recover from Buyer and Duke shall
      hold Buyer harmless from any costs associated with CCR that has been relocated for
      storage and/or otherwise remediated as part of CCR Compliance Activities. However,

                                                29
       Buyer shall pay for the ongoing operations, maintenance, and monitoring costs for CCR
      remediated by Duke, its contractors and/or agents, and which is located at an
      impoundment or landfill owned by Duke.

              6.5.3 Limitations on Disallowances. Except as set forth in Sections 6.5.1 and
      6.5.2, Buyer agrees that it shall not receive, and Buyer hereby irrevocably waives any
      right to receive or seek to receive, any cost treatment, rate methodology, disallowance,
      and/or the benefit of any CCR Costs that Duke is prohibited from recovering and/or are
      not approved or accepted for recovery for any reason by the NCUC, PSCSC, and/or
      FERC; provided however, Duke shall not re-allocate for recovery from Buyer the portion
      of such CCR Costs that Duke has been prohibited from recovering and does not recover
      from any other retail or wholesale customer as a result of such rulings by the NCUC,
      PSCSC, and/or FERC.

6.6     Charges for CPRE Costs. Buyer agrees that Duke shall be entitled to permitted recovery
of the CPRE Costs as outlined in the Rate Formulas.

6.7     IRA Tax Credit Benefits. Duke shall use Commercially Reasonable Efforts to apply any
earned IRA Tax Credits to reduce Duke’s (or its Affiliates’) tax liability for a particular tax year.
Should the IRA Tax Credits exceed Duke’s tax liability for such tax year, Duke shall use
Commercially Reasonable Efforts to sell or transfer any remaining IRA Tax Credits to a third
party. Duke may, in its sole discretion, sell or transfer such earned IRA Tax Credits at a
discounted rate in any Year, including one (1) or more Years following the particular tax year in
which such credits are earned. In the Year after such IRA Tax Credits are monetized, Duke shall
pay to Buyer an amount equal to (i) with respect to earned and monetized IRA PTCs, the
Monthly Credit for Buyer’s IRA PTC Benefit and (ii) with respect to earned and monetized IRA
ITCs, an amount for Buyer’s IRA ITC Benefit, which shall be included in the Rate Formulas.
Calculations of Buyer’s IRA PTC Benefit for any applicable tax year shall be provided to Buyer
in accordance with Section 6.9 and Exhibit IV. Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to
the contrary, if FERC, in accepting, approving, or permitting Duke’s forthcoming filing
proposing implementation of Buyer’s IRA PTC Benefit and Buyer’s IRA ITC Benefit, requires
modification of any provision of this Agreement relating to the calculation of Buyer’s IRA PTC
Benefit or Buyer’s IRA ITC Benefit, or the allocation, treatment, or recovery thereof, Duke may
modify such provision(s) to the extent necessary to conform to the requirements of FERC’s order
solely to the extent required by FERC in such order.

6.8    Transmission and Generator Step-Up Transformer Losses.

              6.8.1 General. For the purpose of calculating energy delivered and demand
      hereunder, quantities shall be at the generator level, i.e., grossed up for all transmission
      losses and generator step-up transformer losses which are incurred between the point of
      generation and the point of interconnection of the Transmission System and Buyer’s
      distribution system. The loss factor used in such calculations shall be the sum of (i) the
      Real Power Loss factor in the DEC Zone as stated in the Transmission Provider’s OATT,
      as it may be amended from time to time, and (ii) the GSU Loss Factor as determined
      under Section 6.8.2.


                                                 30
               6.8.2 GSU Loss Factor. After each Year, Duke shall calculate the applicable
      GSU Loss Factor in accordance with the Attachment W Methodology for Calculation of
      Real Power Loss Factor in Duke’s Open Access Transmission Tariff. By April 1 of the
      Year immediately succeeding the twelve (12)-Month loss factor calculation period, Duke
      shall give notice to Buyer stating the revised GSU Loss Factor (the “Revised GSU Loss
      Factor”) along with supporting calculations and documentation in sufficient detail to
      enable Buyer to verify the accuracy of the Revised GSU Loss Factor. The Revised GSU
      Loss Factor shall be effective June 1st following the giving of such notice. The Revised
      GSU Loss Factor shall be subject to Buyer’s audit rights as set forth in Section 10.4.

6.9    Annual True-Up.

             6.9.1 Estimated Charges. Duke shall provide Buyer its estimated Monthly
      Demand Rate, estimated System Average Energy Rate, estimated Monthly Charge for
      Buyer’s CCR Costs, and the estimated Monthly Credit for Buyer’s IRA PTC Benefit for
      the succeeding Year by December 1st of the current Year, each of which will be subject to
      annual true-up as set forth in this Section 6.9.

              6.9.2 Annual True-Up. Following the end of each Year, Duke shall reconcile the
      estimated charges and credits billed with the actual charges and credits for that Year. The
      net difference between the estimated amounts and the actual amounts shall be the “Annual
      True-Up Amount”. The Monthly Demand Rate, the Monthly Billing Demand, the
      Ancillary Services Credits, the System Average Energy Rate, the Monthly Charge for
      Buyer’s CCR Costs, and the Monthly Credit for Buyer’s IRA PTC Benefit each shall be
      trued-up annually after actual data for such Year becomes available. Duke shall provide
      the preliminary true-up data to Buyer no later than June 15 following the Year in which
      the Partial Requirements Service was provided, and shall provide the actual true-up data
      to Buyer on or about July 1 following such Year.

              6.9.3 True-Up of Monthly Charge for Buyer’s CCR Costs. CCR Disallowances
      that are ordered or determined under an applicable Law that are related to a Year in which
      the annual true-up for the System Average Energy Rate and/or the Monthly Charge for
      Buyer’s CCR Costs has already occurred shall be adjusted in accordance with Section
      IV.A of Exhibit III. Adjustments for such additional CCR Disallowances shall survive
      termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 13.10.

6.10 Payment of Annual True-Up Amount. The Annual True-Up Amount shall be paid or
credited along with the Monthly statement in accordance with the billing and payment provisions
in Article 10. To the extent that the Buyer selects the lump sum payment option as set forth in
Section 6.11.1, such lump sum payment shall be included in the June statement, which will be
issued during the first week of July, and it will be payable on July 20th.

            6.10.1 Refund. If the Annual True-Up Amount reflects that estimated charges
      exceeded actual charges, then Duke shall refund the difference to Buyer as a lump sum.

            6.10.2 Surcharge. If the Annual True-Up Amount reflects that actual charges
      exceeded estimated charges, then Buyer shall pay the difference to Duke as a lump sum.

                                              31
                6.10.3 Interest. The Annual True-Up Amount shall include interest payable by
       Buyer or Duke, as applicable, on any refunds or surcharges calculated at the Interest Rate
       from the date on which the overpayment or underpayment was made to the date on which
       the refund or surcharge is due and paid.

6.11   Installment Payment Option.

               6.11.1 Buyer’s Election. Following delivery of the actual true-up data pursuant
       to Section 6.9, Buyer may elect to pay the Annual True-Up Amount surcharge or receive
       the Annual True-Up Amount refund (as applicable), either in a lump sum or in twelve
       (12) equal Monthly installments payments (“Installment Payment Option”). In the
       event Buyer desires to elect the Installment Payment Option, Buyer must notify Duke, in
       writing, within ten (10) Business Days of receiving the actual true-up data under Section
       6.9. If Buyer does not timely notify Duke of such election, Buyer shall be deemed to
       have elected lump sum payments or credits, as applicable, in accordance with Section
       6.10.

               6.11.2 Limitations. The Installment Payment Option is subject to the following
       limitations:

               6.11.2.1        The twelve (12) Monthly installments will be made in equal
               amounts for the ensuing twelve (12)-Month period, which begins with the June
               bill each Year, shall not extend beyond the May bill of the following Year;

               6.11.2.2       The (12) Monthly installment amounts shall include interest
               payable at the Interest Rate from the date on which the overpayment or
               underpayment was made to the date on which the refund or surcharge is due and
               paid; provided, however, Duke shall only pay interest on a refund under the lump
               sum payment or the Installment Payment Option until July 20th of each Year,
               which is the due date for the lump sum payment, even if Buyer chooses to receive
               a refund under the Installment Payment Option;

               6.11.2.3       Unless otherwise agreed upon by Duke in writing in its sole
               discretion, the amount of the true-up that Buyer may pay back to Duke over a
               maximum twelve-Month period is limited to an amount not to exceed five percent
               (5%) of the Buyer’s total annual billings, and the Buyer must pay the excess (>
               five percent (5%) of total annual billed amounts) in a lump sum payment in the
               June bill; and

               6.11.2.4      Duke has the right to revoke the Installment Payment Option and
               require a lump sum payment for the true-up if the Buyer does not maintain timely
               payment history.

                    Article 7 - Transmission, Energy Imbalance, and RTO

7.1    Transmission Arrangements. Duke shall be responsible for making all arrangements
necessary and paying for all costs incurred under contractual arrangements necessary to transmit
the electric energy provided hereunder to the NCEMC Large Load 1 Delivery Points. Buyer
                                               32
 shall be responsible for making and paying for all contractual arrangements with the
Transmission Provider necessary for the transmission of the electric energy provided hereunder
from the NCEMC Large Load 1 Delivery Points. This Agreement does not obligate Duke to
provide, pay for, or make arrangements for, any Transmission Services. Duke shall have no
responsibility for any costs incurred in connection with the construction of any transmission
and/or distribution facilities necessary for delivery of energy to NCEMC Large Load 1 Delivery
Points.

7.2    Energy Imbalance. Duke shall reimburse Buyer for any Hour in which, as a result of
Duke’s delivery of an amount of energy less than the NCEMC Large Load 1 Load (unless
excused under this Agreement), Energy Imbalance Service charges are incurred by Buyer in
accordance with the Transmission Provider’s OATT. Buyer shall reimburse Duke for any Hour
in which, as a result of Duke’s delivery of an amount of energy in excess of the NCEMC Large
Load 1 Load, Energy Imbalance Service compensation is provided to Buyer in accordance with
the Transmission Provider’s OATT.

7.3     Regional Transmission Organization. If an ISO, RTO, independent transmission
company or other future organization, agency or authority is approved by FERC to serve as the
Transmission Provider in replacement of Duke Transmission, then Duke and Buyer will
reasonably cooperate to make or enter into replacement arrangements with such entity to the
extent required in connection with the implementation of this Agreement. The Parties expressly
acknowledge and agree that neither the implementation of an ISO, RTO, independent
transmission company or other future organization, agency or authority that has been approved
by FERC to serve as the Transmission Provider nor the failure of the Parties to enter into the
arrangements contemplated under this Section 7.3 shall relieve either Party of any obligations
under this Agreement.

              7.3.1 Cost Responsibility. Buyer expressly acknowledges and agrees that
      nothing herein shall be construed to in any way relieve Buyer of, or impose upon Duke,
      the responsibility for any fees, costs, or charges (including congestion costs, transmission
      losses, or the costs or charges to secure financial transmission rights or the equivalent
      thereof) that may be imposed on Buyer by an ISO, RTO, independent transmission
      company or other future organization, agency or authority that has been approved by
      FERC to serve as the Transmission Provider in connection with Transmission Service or
      Ancillary Services. The Parties expressly acknowledge and agree that neither Party shall
      have any right or interest in any financial transmission rights, congestion revenue rights,
      or other financial rights to firm transmission as may be defined or authorized by
      regulatory authority that are allocated to, assigned to, transferred to or acquired by the
      other Party.

              7.3.2 Interpretation with FERC Orders. Each Party conducts and shall conduct
      its operations in a manner intended to comply with FERC Order No. 717, Standards of
      Conduct for Transmission Providers, and its companion orders, requiring the separation of
      its transmission and merchant functions. Moreover, the Parties acknowledge that Duke
      Transmission offers transmission service on its system in a manner intended to comply
      with FERC policies and requirements relating to the provision of open-access
      transmission service. Buyer expressly recognizes that for purposes hereof Duke

                                               33
       Transmission shall be deemed to be a separate entity and separate contracting party from
      Duke. Buyer acknowledges that Duke, acting in its merchant capacity function hereunder,
      has no responsibility for or control over Duke Transmission, and is not liable for any
      breach of agreement or duty by Duke Transmission or any other Transmission Provider.
      The Parties acknowledge and agree that all arrangements for transmission shall be
      separate and free-standing contracts and that the terms hereof are not binding upon Duke

                               Article 8 - Operating Committee

8.1     Operating Committee. The Parties shall establish an “Operating Committee” consisting
of one (1) Representative each. The Operating Committee shall act only by mutual agreement or
consent. Duke and Buyer shall designate their respective Representatives to the Operating
Committee, plus any alternate, by written notice delivered in accordance with Section 13.21
within thirty (30) Days after the Execution Date. Each Party’s Representative on the Operating
Committee is authorized to act on behalf of such Party with respect to any matter arising under
this Agreement.

8.2    Duties of the Operating Committee. The Operating Committee shall facilitate the
coordination and interaction between the Parties with respect to the performance of the duties
and obligations imposed on the Parties hereunder, including development or revision of
appropriate protocols and procedures therefor. The Operating Committee shall not, however,
have any authority to modify or otherwise alter the Parties’ rights and obligations under this
Agreement.

                                 Article 10 - Billing and Payment

10.1 Billing Period. Unless otherwise specifically provided in this Agreement or agreed upon
by the Parties in writing, the Month shall be the standard period for determining all billings and
payments under this Agreement.

10.2   Billing Statements.


                                                 35
               10.2.1 Initial Statements. After the end of each Billing Period, Duke shall deliver
      to Buyer a statement setting forth for the Billing Period (i) the sum of the electric energy
      delivered for all Hours during that Billing Period, and (ii) Duke’s calculation of any
      amounts due from Buyer under this Agreement for the Billing Period (“Billing
      Statement”). Notwithstanding the foregoing, Duke’s failure to render a statement as set
      forth above shall not relieve Buyer from its obligation to make payment when such
      statement is rendered, provided such statement is rendered within twelve (12) Months
      after the end of the Billing Period provided, however, such twelve (12) Month limitation

      billings will be made on an estimated basis. In addition, the Parties agree that after-the-

      available funds by electronic funds transfer, or by other mutually agreeable method, to the

      payment may be withheld pursuant to Section 10.3, not paid by the due date shall be

      calculated from the due date to the date the delinquent amount is paid in full.

             perform any obligation to, Buyer shall not excuse Buyer from any obligation to
             pay Duke, or perform any other obligation imposed upon Buyer under this
             Agreement.

 (b) specifies the amount in dispute (the “Disputed Amount”) and (c) provides documentation

                        Article 12 –Credit and Collateral Requirements

12.1 Material Adverse Change. Each of the Parties shall be deemed to have experienced a
material adverse change (“MAC”) if it is no longer Creditworthy.

12.2 Notice. Each Party shall provide the other Party written notice within two (2) Business
Days of the occurrence of a MAC affecting the notifying Party or of the occurrence of any event
that may reasonably cause a MAC.

12.3 Performance Assurance. To protect either Party against potential default of payment or
performance, any Party that experiences a MAC shall post as Performance Assurance in an
amount equal to the highest two (2) Months of Duke’s billings under this Agreement for the
previous twelve (12) Months. Such Performance Assurance shall be provided by the Party
experiencing the MAC in a cash deposit or letters of credit from a financial institution
reasonably acceptable to the Party not experiencing the MAC within five (5) Business Days after
the date on which the MAC occurs. Any letter of credit shall be in a form satisfactory to the
Party not experiencing the MAC in its sole commercially reasonable discretion. If the
Performance Assurance is in the form of a letter of credit, the Party experiencing the MAC (“the
posting Party”) will ensure that the letter of credit remains in full force, outstanding and in the
required amount through the term of this Agreement. The letter of credit shall provide that if (i) the
letter of credit is within thirty (30) days of expiration and (ii) the posting Party has failed to renew
or replace the letter of credit pursuant to the terms of this section, then the Party not experiencing
the MAC (“the other Party”) may draw and retain the full amount of the letter of credit to be held
as security for the posting Party’s obligations under this Agreement. If at any time the rating of the
issuer of the letter of credit falls below A- with S&P or A3 with Moody’s and the posting Party fails
to replace the letter of credit with Performance Assurance in accordance with this Agreement within
five (5) Business Days, then the other Party shall be entitled to draw and retain the full amount of
the letter of credit.

        If the posting Party has provided a letter of credit as Performance Assurance and
subsequently desires to replace it with a cash deposit, the posting Party, upon written notice to the
other Party, may substitute the Performance Assurance with a cash deposit, or if the posting Party
has provided a cash deposit and subsequently desires to replace it with a letter of credit, the posting
Party, upon written notice to the other Party, may substitute the Performance Assurance with a letter
of credit conforming to the requirements of this Agreement. If the posting Party elects to provide
such substitute Performance Assurance, the other Party will return to the posting Party (or to the
Issuing Bank if a letter of credit) the Performance Assurance previously provided upon receipt of
the replacement Performance Assurance.

12.4 Security Interest in Cash Deposit. To the extent that a posting Party delivers
Performance Assurance hereunder in the form of a cash deposit, the posting Party hereby grants

                                                  39
 to the other Party a present and continuing security interest in, and lien on (and right of netting
and set-off against), and assignment of, such Performance Assurance, including, without
limitation, cash collateral and cash equivalent collateral and any and all proceeds resulting
therefrom or the liquidation thereof, whether now or hereafter held by, on behalf of, or for the
benefit of, the other Party; and agrees to take such action as the other Party reasonably requires
to perfect the other Party’s first-priority security interest in, and lien on (and right of netting and
set-off against), such Performance Assurance and any and all proceeds resulting therefrom or
from the liquidation thereof.

12.5 Interest on Cash Used as Collateral. If cash collateral is posted, the Party holding the
cash collateral shall pay interest to the posting Party at the Federal Funds Effective Rate. The
Federal Funds Effective Rate is the rate for that day opposite the caption “Federal Funds
(Effective)” as set forth in the weekly statistical release designated as H.15(519), or any
successor publication published by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. The
posting Party shall invoice the other Party for interest accrued during the previous Month and the
other Party shall pay such amount within ten (10) days of receipt of such invoice.

12.6 Continuing Nature of Collateral Requirement. The posting Party must continue to post
the collateral until the MAC is cured. The other Party shall have the right to draw upon, use, and
dispose of all collateral that is posted under Section 12.3, if the posting Party fails to fulfill any
of its payment or performance obligations under this Agreement, and such failure shall constitute
an Event of Default. In the event any collateral is drawn upon by the other Party in accordance
with the provisions of this Section 12.6, the posting Party shall within three (3) Business Days
fully replenish the collateral to the monetary amount required by Section 12.3.

12.7 Information. During each year of this Agreement, Duke shall provide Buyer a copy of
Duke’s annual report and Form 10K, and any amendments thereto, within thirty (30) days after

amendment. Buyer shall provide Duke with a copy of Buyer’s complete annual audited

              13.12.1 Capacity Rate Information. Each June 15, Duke will provide an estimate
      for the Duke Formula Rate for Capacity for the subsequent five (5) calendar years,
      including underlying calculations and supporting workable Excel files. Also on each June
      15, Duke will provide an estimate for only the Duke Formula Rate for Capacity for
      calendar years six (6) through ten (10). Each December 1, Duke will provide an estimate
      for the Duke Formula Rate for Capacity for the subsequent five (5) years which will be
      used for Monthly billing subject to true-up when actual costs are available as described in
      Section 6.9.

              13.12.2 System Average Energy Rate Information. No later than December 1 of
      each calendar year, Duke shall provide to Buyer the System Average Energy Rate, in
      $/MWh, for use in the next calendar year and a forecast for the next five (5) years. At
      approximately mid-year of the calendar year that service is provided, or at another date
      mutually agreed to by the Parties, the Parties will review the estimated System Average
      Energy Rate and consider if an adjustment to the estimated System Average Energy Rate
      is desired to more closely approximate the expected System Average Energy Rate for the
      subject year. If the Parties agree, Duke will adjust the estimated System Average Energy
      Rate to the agreed upon estimate until such time as the true-up is implemented.

               Duke agrees to perform periodic reviews for the calculation of the System Average
      Energy Rate for the subject calendar year. Duke shall informally communicate, via e-mail
      or telephone, the results of this review to Buyer with a current estimate of calendar year-
      end Energy Charges. In the event that the current estimate does not change by a Material
      Amount, the estimate shall remain the same until such time as the estimate does change by
      a Material Amount. For the purpose of this Agreement, a “Material Amount” shall be an
      amount greater than one percent (1%).

              13.12.3 System Average Energy Rate Forecast, Fuel Mix and Hedging
      Information. By June 15 of each calendar year, Duke shall provide Buyer a forecast for a
      period of not less than five (5) calendar years, of the System Average Energy Rate with
      sufficient detail to demonstrate individual components of the System Average System
      Average Energy Rate, including, but not limited to expected fuel mix, the hedged fuel
      amount, hedged fuel prices, emission amounts and allowances, and assumptions used in
      the development of this forecast. For these forecasted rates, the estimated rates will
      reflect the expected annual energy related costs as well as the corresponding annual net
      generated and purchased MWh for that calendar year. Also on each June 15, Duke will
      provide an estimate for the System Average Energy Rate only for calendar years six (6)
      through ten (10). The Parties will review the forecast information and explore options to
      manage Buyer’s cost volatility. Duke will assist Buyer in evaluating opportunities for an
      expanded hedging program. Duke also agrees to provide, on a quarterly basis, the current
      year drivers of the System Average Energy Rate.
